easy.def: To change something a little to make it better.
examples: I tweaked my drawing.
She tweaked the recipe.
Tweak the plan.

more.def: To make a small change to something to improve it.
examples: I tweaked my story to make the ending better.
She tweaked the recipe by adding a little more cinnamon.
The coach tweaked the plan before the game.

easy.def: The short, high sound a small bird makes.
examples: I heard a tweet in the tree.
The bird gave a tweet.
A tweet came from the nest.

more.def: The short, high sound made by a small bird, or a short message posted online.
examples: A tweet came from the nest in the tree.
The robin's tweet woke me at sunrise.
We heard the soft tweet of baby birds.

easy.def: To make a short, high bird sound.
examples: The bird will tweet.
Baby birds tweet for food.
A robin tweeted at dawn.

more.def: To make a short, high sound like a small bird.
examples: The little birds tweeted from the branch.
A robin tweets loudly every morning outside my window.
The chicks tweeted when their mother came back.

easy.def: The number 12.
examples: I have twelve crayons.
There are twelve eggs in a dozen.
It is twelve o'clock.

more.def: The number that comes after eleven, written 12.
examples: There are twelve months in a year.
A dozen is twelve.
The clock struck twelve at noon.

easy.def: Number twenty in order.
examples: I am twentieth in line.
It is his twentieth birthday.
The twentieth page is torn.

more.def: Coming after nineteen others in order.
examples: I finished in twentieth place in the long race.
Grandpa is celebrating his twentieth wedding day.
The twentieth day of June is the start of summer.

easy.def: The number after nineteen.
examples: I have twenty coins.
Count to twenty.
Twenty kids are in the room.

more.def: The number 20, which is two tens.
examples: Twenty minutes later, the bread was ready.
She saved twenty dollars to buy a book.
Count by twos up to twenty.

easy.def: Two times.
examples: I knocked twice.
He read it twice.
I went to the park twice.

more.def: Two times, or two times as much.
examples: I rang the doorbell twice.
She read the book twice.
The pool is twice as deep as the tub.

easy.def: A small, thin branch.
examples: The bird carried a twig.
I snapped a twig.
A twig fell.

more.def: A small, thin branch of a tree or a bush.
examples: The bird carried a twig to build its nest.
We collected twigs to light the campfire.
I snapped a dry twig in two.

easy.def: The soft light after the sun goes down.
examples: We played outside at twilight.
The sky was pink at twilight.
Bats come out at twilight.

more.def: The faint, soft light in the sky just after sunset, before it gets completely dark.
examples: At twilight, the sky turned purple and the first stars appeared.
Bats flew out of the cave as twilight settled over the valley.
We walked home slowly in the twilight.

easy.def: One of two children born at the same time to the same mother.
examples: My sister has a twin.
The twins look alike.
He is my twin.

more.def: One of two people or animals who were born together to the same mother.
examples: The twins wore matching shirts.
She has a twin brother in the same class.
The twin lambs followed their mother.

easy.def: To shine with little flashes of light.
examples: The stars twinkle.
Her eyes twinkled.
The lights twinkled.

more.def: To shine with small, quick flashes of light.
examples: The stars twinkle in the night sky.
Her eyes twinkled when she smiled.
The lights on the tree twinkled in the dark room.

easy.def: A small, quick flash of light.
examples: I saw a twinkle in the sky.
He had a twinkle in his eye.
The twinkle was bright.

more.def: A tiny, sparkling light that comes and goes.
examples: I saw a twinkle in the sky and made a wish.
He had a twinkle in his eye when he told the joke.
The twinkle of the lights made the room feel happy.

related.def: Shining with little flashes of light.

easy.def: To spin around and around.
examples: She twirled in her dress.
I twirl my baton.
The skater twirled.

more.def: To turn around and around quickly, or to make something spin.
examples: She twirled in her new dress until she got dizzy.
The cook twirled spaghetti around a fork.
He twirled the baton in the air and caught it.

easy.def: A fast spin.
examples: She did a twirl.
The dancer made a twirl.
A twirl of the skirt.

more.def: A quick, turning movement around in a circle.
examples: The dancer finished with a graceful twirl.
With a twirl, she showed off her new skirt.
He gave the baton a twirl.

easy.def: To turn something around.
examples: Twist the lid.
She twisted the cap.
I twisted my ankle.

more.def: To turn something around, or to bend it in a curve.
examples: Twist the lid to open the jar.
She twisted the wire into a heart shape.
He twisted his ankle on the ice.

easy.def: A turn in a story.
examples: The story had a twist.
The twist was a surprise.
The movie has a twist at the end.

more.def: A surprising turn in the way events go.
examples: The story had a surprise twist at the end.
The road has a twist near the bridge.
The twist in the plot made everyone gasp.

easy.def: A strong spinning wind storm, also called a tornado.
examples: A twister hit the town.
The twister spun.
We hid from the twister.

more.def: A very strong storm with a funnel of wind that spins very fast, also called a tornado.
examples: A twister swept across the plains and tore up trees.
We went to the cellar when we heard the twister warning.
The twister lasted only a few minutes.

easy.def: To make a quick little movement that you do not plan.
examples: My eye twitches.
The rabbit's nose twitched.
The cat's tail twitches.

more.def: To move or jerk suddenly with a quick, small movement.
examples: My eye twitches when I am tired.
The rabbit's nose twitched as it smelled the carrot.
The sleeping dog's legs twitched as it dreamed.

easy.def: A quick little movement of a muscle.
examples: I felt a twitch in my eye.
The twitch was small.
There was a twitch in his nose.

more.def: A sudden, quick movement of a muscle.
examples: I felt a twitch in my eyelid.
A twitch of the cat's ear showed that it heard something.
He gave a little twitch and then smiled.

easy.def: The number 2.
examples: I have two eyes.
Two plus two is four.
She has two cats.

more.def: The number 2, which is one more than one.
examples: A bicycle has two wheels.
We saw two eagles circling over the canyon.
The twins turned two on Tuesday.
